main_text.p: talis, quod non agatur de capite aut vitâ cujusquam? Insuper, quis inficias iverit duellum appellari posse, si latro vel nocturnus agrorum depopulator aliquem viatorem in itinere aggrediatur? Aut si ex improviso duo nocturno tempore, in se mutuò irruant? Nulla tamen hinc inde deliberatio, nulla intentio dimicandi, nec animo destinato conflictus instituitur, verùm casu prorsus inopinato. Amplius, quid si duo loco designato, indicto tempore, irâ incitante, & ut vindictæ cupidini satisfaciant, invicem adoriantur, an non singulare certamen esse dicetur, licet nec ad innocentiæ purgationem, nec ad gloriam quicquam conferat hoc duelli genus, neque quidem ex intentione dimicantium?
Eligius Bassæus in Floribus Theoclog. pag. 264.Ab hâc Lignani descriptione non multum recedit Eligius

page.notes: The marginal note at left is set in small type and runs across the last lines of the page; it is placed at the start of the final paragraph. Long s has been written as plain s throughout (e.g. "destinato", "instituitur", "descriptione"). The word "Baf-" at the lower right is the catchword, shown as "Bassæus" with the hyphen dropped; the final line of text ends at "Eligius". The line-end hyphens in "dimi-cantium", "ag-grediatur", "de capi-te" and "Flori-bus" are joined in the transcription.
